evidence: User cohorts; entitlements; student/staff separation; shared-device model; guest and lifecycle policies.
procedure: Separate staff, students, minors where applicable, temporary workers and shared devices in sampling. Confirm actual SKU capability and approved privacy obligations. Test rapid turnover, shared-session cleanup and resource access without assuming enterprise defaults.
criterion: Population-specific requirements are explicit and supported by evidence; business convenience does not silently exempt a cohort.
falsification: A shared workstation retains a previous user's organizational session or a seasonal account survives termination.
remediation: Correct shared-session and lifecycle procedures; obtain accountable policy decisions for each population.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.

title: Multi-Geo and residency verification
objective: Test data-location commitments at the relevant service boundary.
applicability: Multi-Geo, ADR and regulated residency requirements.
evidence: Contractual commitments; data-location reports; user/site geography; migrations; backup and third-party locations.
procedure: Map each requirement to the exact workload and data category. Distinguish storage from processing and support access. Verify current versus committed locations, pending moves and external copies.
criterion: Evidence supports the particular residency claim; tenant home geography is not used as proof for all data.
falsification: A backup, connector or analytics export resides outside the stated workload boundary.
remediation: Resolve location gaps or amend the approved architecture and disclosures with responsible owners.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.

title: Loop and SharePoint Embedded
objective: Include content outside ordinary site inventory assumptions.
applicability: Loop and applications using SharePoint Embedded containers.
evidence: Workspace/container inventory; storage location; app permissions; owners; retention/hold capabilities.
procedure: Identify actual storage for each content type and creator experience. Verify membership, lifecycle, retention and eDiscovery against current capability tables. Test a synthetic artifact through discovery and authorized access; do not assume all storage variants behave identically.
criterion: Containers and workspaces are governed and included in evidence/recovery scope, with current limitations recorded.
falsification: A compliance search covers ordinary sites but misses a synthetic item in an application container.
remediation: Add container-aware inventory and procedures; restrict unsupported use cases if required.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.

title: Forms and public intake
objective: Control information collected and shared through forms.
applicability: Microsoft Forms and equivalent externally published intake.
evidence: Form inventory; external response/collaboration settings; response access; owner; data purpose and exports.
procedure: Sample public forms, sensitive questions and response exports. Verify ownership transfer, respondent identity needs, anonymous access and collaboration links. Trace stored responses and connected automation to their retention and access controls.
criterion: Public intake collects only approved information and response data has an authorized audience and lifecycle.
falsification: An external collaborator can read response data through a forgotten sharing path.
remediation: Narrow form sharing and response access; assign owners and document disposal.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.

title: Other enabled productivity workloads
objective: Avoid silently omitting smaller services.
applicability: Planner, Bookings, Viva, Sway, Whiteboard, Stream, Project and additional enabled services.
evidence: Enabled-service inventory; owners; feature documentation; sharing; data storage; integration and recovery scope.
procedure: For every enabled service, complete the workload worksheet: identity, sharing, storage, licensing, retention, audit and recovery. Identify its backing services and verify current product-specific documentation before issuing a result. Escalate unsupported assumptions as scope gaps.
criterion: No enabled workload is silently omitted. This generic overlay is a scoping procedure, not a product-specific configuration certification.
falsification: Choose a service absent from the main scanner and ask for its stored-data and recovery owner.
remediation: Add a tailored assessment module with primary documentation; record Not assessed until sufficient evidence exists.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.

title: Mergers and multiple tenants
objective: Assess trust and data movement across organizational boundaries.
applicability: Acquisitions, divestitures and multi-tenant organizations.
evidence: Tenant inventory; cross-tenant relationships; migrations; dual identities; delegated roles; data ownership.
procedure: Review who retains access before, during and after transition. Inspect partner-specific trust, cross-tenant synchronization and migration service accounts. Reconcile retention and evidence obligations before decommissioning.
criterion: Trust, data ownership and access removal are planned and evidenced for each transition phase.
falsification: An acquired tenant's admin retains a migration credential after cutover.
remediation: Expire transitional access and verify source/destination controls before closure.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.

title: Regulated control overlay and formal assurance
objective: Translate a framework engagement into defensible testing.
applicability: Contractual or regulated audits requiring a specified framework/version.
evidence: Authoritative requirements; formal scope; framework version; mapping; evidence; assessor requirements.
procedure: Map each applicable requirement to one or more control tests and identify uncovered clauses. Have qualified owners interpret legal requirements. Validate technical evidence, process operation and provider/customer boundaries separately.
criterion: Any conformity claim matches the authorized assessment standard, scope, period and assessor role; this playbook alone confers no certification.
falsification: A completed Microsoft recommendation is used to claim satisfaction of an unrelated legal clause.
remediation: Complete the missing mapping, interpretation or assessment and qualify interim reporting.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.

title: Virtual desktops and Cloud PCs
objective: Include hosted endpoints in identity and device assurance.
applicability: Windows 365, Azure Virtual Desktop and shared virtual endpoints.
evidence: Hosted desktop inventory; identity model; policies; images; administrator access; recovery dependencies.
procedure: Apply endpoint and access tests to hosted desktops, including image lifecycle, local data, redirection and privileged sessions. Validate product-specific configuration against current primary documentation before scoring the deployment.
criterion: Hosted endpoints are included in coverage and recovery; omitted product-specific checks remain Not assessed.
falsification: A privileged Cloud PC is assumed safe because it is hosted but lacks the intended endpoint controls.
remediation: Extend device management and recovery coverage and commission a specific platform review where needed.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.

title: Network and access dependencies
objective: Validate DNS, connectivity and secure access dependencies.
applicability: All tenants; enhanced review for proxies and remote access.
evidence: DNS ownership; proxy/VPN architecture; trusted locations; certificates; availability monitoring.
procedure: Trace administrator and user connectivity to authentication and workloads. Review who controls DNS and named locations; identify proxy bypass and authentication dependencies. Test a representative outage or alternate access path under an approved plan.
criterion: Critical connectivity has owners and recovery plans; network location alone is not treated as strong identity assurance.
falsification: A broad trusted IP range unintentionally includes an untrusted user or partner path.
remediation: Narrow assumptions and align network/access design with observed authentication behavior.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.

title: Accessibility and control usability
objective: Keep required protection usable for the intended workforce.
applicability: Authentication, device restrictions and collaboration controls.
evidence: Exception requests; accessible authentication options; helpdesk trends; pilot results; training.
procedure: Review whether users with differing devices, connectivity or accessibility needs can use approved controls. Test representative personas and recovery paths. Track repeated support workarounds as evidence of a design gap.
criterion: Protection remains effective and usable for legitimate users; workarounds do not create permanent unowned bypasses.
falsification: A user can work only after helpdesk repeatedly disables an access control.
remediation: Provide supported alternatives and improve rollout/training while preserving the required objective.
cadence: At initial audit and after material change; periodic review based on the approved risk plan.
